summary: Remediated rsyslog drift on node1-node4. All systems now accept TCP syslog on port 5514, route local0 messages to /var/log/infraset-app.log, enforce persistent firewall and SELinux settings, and start rsyslog automatically. Application data remained unchanged through remediation and one-at-a-time node reboots.
actions_performed: Validated the installed rsyslog package and package-file integrity on every node.
Installed and syntax-validated the standard imtcp/local0 configuration.
Enabled and started rsyslog; opened TCP 5514 persistently in firewalld.
Assigned TCP 5514 to syslogd_port_t and corrected the destination log's SELinux context.
Tested TCP local0 delivery using each node's managed IP.
Restarted each node sequentially and verified changed boot identities and full recovery.

evidence.requirement: Correct package, configuration, service, listener, and message routing on all nodes
evidence.summary: Final audits show valid rsyslog packages/configuration, enabled and active services, IPv4/IPv6 listeners on 5514, and successful local0 TCP messages in the required log.

evidence.requirement: Persistent firewall and SELinux security configuration
evidence.summary: TCP 5514 is allowed at runtime and permanently, mapped to syslogd_port_t, and the log has var_log_t context; final audits prove persistence.
Initial and final SHA-256 checksums match exactly on every node, including after restart.
